facts.statement: Basutodon lived during the Late Triassic in the Lower Elliot Formation of Lesotho.
facts.quote: Basutodon is a genus of suchian archosaur from the Late Triassic (late Norian-early Rhaetian) Lower Elliot Formation of Lesotho.

facts.statement: The holotype of Basutodon is a single tooth found near Euskelosaurus browni in the upper Elliot Formation of Lesotho.
facts.quote: The holotype is a single tooth that was discovered alongside the remains of Euskelosaurus browni in the upper Elliot Formation, Lesotho.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Likhoelesaurus ingens may be the same animal as Basutodon ferox.
facts.quote: "Likhoelesaurus ingens", an undescribed archosauriform from the Lower Elliot Formation of South Africa, may have been the same animal as Basutodon ferox.

facts.statement: Basutodon is currently classified as a basal member of Suchia, though some researchers suggest it may belong to Rauisuchia.
facts.quote: Basutodon is currently listed as a basal member of Suchia, although Tolchard et al. (2019) suggested that Basutodon may belong to Rauisuchia.

facts.statement: Basutodon was a pseudosuchian archosaur that lived in the Lower Elliot Formation of Lesotho.
facts.quote: Basutodon era un género de arcosaurio pseudosuquio que vivió a finales del Carniense - principios del Noriense en el piso inferior de la Formación Elliot del Triásico Superior en Lesoto.

facts.statement: Basutodon lived between 227.3 and 201.4 million years ago during the Norian to Rhaetian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Rhaetian (227.3 to 201.4 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The species Basutodon ferox was named and described by von Huene in 1932.
rejected.quote: The species Basutodon ferox was named and described by von Huene (1932).
